requirement:
The generated coverage subchapter MUST make coverage-collection and
post-suite-checking guidance available under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance`, without requiring
separate authored content.
rationale:
The subject requires the generated coverage subchapter to carry the coverage-collection and post-suite-checking guidance described by `requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance`. That guidance must not depend on separately authored content.

The test `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It starts from a fixture whose parent chapter holds only a heading, so no authored coverage content exists. It calls `populate_in`, takes the generated `coverage` chapter, and asserts that `coverage.content` contains each of these strings:
- `habeas test`
- `habeas coverage -- --workspace`
- `habeas coverage-check`
- the "run `habeas coverage-check` as a separate step" wording after the instrumented run succeeds
- the statement that `habeas test` collects coverage for the whole workspace and then checks it
- the statement that the static validation test needs no prior coverage

It also asserts several other guidance phrases. These cover the 80% target, `habeas:coverage` citations, accepted review, and the absence of any project declaration or special configuration.

I read the `GUIDANCE` constant in `src/execution_coverage.rs`. It contains these phrases, so the assertions check the real generated text. The test runs with both numbered and unnumbered parents, so the guidance appears in both generated forms.

The test checks that the guidance is present in the generated chapter. That is the obligation here. The exact content of the guidance belongs to `check.guidance`, which is cited context and not reassessed. I found no gap.
